The Stoney Lake example study, prepared for the mortality rules

Source: R/mortality_bands.R
example_mortality.Rd

detqc_example after the steps of vignette("mortality-review"): calibrate_sensors() converts the depth readings of ST-02 and ST-03 to metres, filter_post_release() removes the first 6 hours after release (106 detections) and filter_min_lag() at 4,500 s removes 43 isolated detections. A fourth table gives the true fate of each animal: ST-02 dies at 02:00 UTC on 4 June 2024 and its tag is then heard only at station S011; the other three live to the end of the record. No real data are included with the package.

Usage

example_mortality

Format

A list of four data frames:

detections

3,148 detections, with the columns of detqc_example$detections and the depth in metres in sensor_value.

deployments

the 20 deployments of detqc_example.

animals

the 4 animals of detqc_example.

fates

one row per animal: animal_id, fate ("alive" or "dead") and death_datetime (UTC).

Source

Built by https://github.com/jakebrownscombe/detqc/blob/main/data-raw/detqc_example.R, which is in the repository and not in the installed package.

Details

The default rules of mortality_rules() read final runs of 14 days, and the study runs from 2 to 10 June 2024, so they send all four animals to review. Scaled to the study, as in the example below, they band ST-02 dead.

Examples

study <- example_mortality
dets <- detset(study$detections, study$deployments, study$animals)
# Rules scaled to a study of 2 to 10 June 2024
mort_rules <- mortality_rules(min_days = 3, min_calendar_days = 3,
                         min_flat_days = 2, within_days = 2)
bands <- detect_mortality(dets, rules = mort_rules)$bands
bands[, c("animal_id", "band", "deciding_rule")]
#>   animal_id   band      deciding_rule
#> 1     ST-02   dead       terminal_run
#> 2     ST-01 review terminal_run_stray
#> 3     ST-03 review         record_end
#> 4     ST-04 review         record_end
study$fates
#>   animal_id  fate      death_datetime
#> 1     ST-01 alive                <NA>
#> 2     ST-02  dead 2024-06-04 02:00:00
#> 3     ST-03 alive                <NA>
#> 4     ST-04 alive                <NA>
